title: Static fallbacks, the orphaned VK SDK and the partial Capacitor bundle
why: Four rows that reach signature with their successor still unnamed — every successor cell reads "to be named". On three of them — `404.html`, `offline.html`, `vkid-sdk.js` — the owner cell is blank as well: it literally reads "no capability named on the inventory row", and that blank cell is the finding. Blank is not the same as having nothing to own: `S-659` is classed KEEP AS CAPABILITY with successor `CAPABILITY_IN_CHAT` and retirement condition "NOT RETIRED — it becomes a capability". The fourth row, `S-490` (`app-tenant.html`), already carries an evidenced owner — StatusBar, Keyboard, App/appUrlOpen and TeamVoicePlayer present, eight further plugins missing including SplashScreen, so the native splash never clears — and it injects `X-Telegram-InitData` at four sites, which makes it identity-bearing and a gated retirement, not a dead file. Only `vkid-sdk.js` is genuinely dead: zero references in `app.html`, `index.html` and `tips.html`, no capability to lose, and its mere presence violates the standing "no VK/MAX" rule (CLAUDE.md gotcha #7); its row also records residue to clear in the same pass — `app-data.json` still carries `"max": "#"` under social. `offline.html` is dead as a mechanism, since the service worker deliberately carries no `fetch` handler and can never serve a fallback, yet it is still live on the host as a deployed artifact.
disappear: Nothing in Wave 1: every retirement in this group is scheduled for K16, and the signature executes none of it. In K16 `vkid-sdk.js` goes — 169,847 bytes of unreferenced third-party code, already retired in practice and removed there in fact — together with the `"max": "#"` residue in `app-data.json`. `offline.html` retires from primary navigation row by row in the same package; because it ships as `app/offline.html` and is recorded in four Beget deploy manifests, that work pulls a live artifact off the host and is not a repository-only delete. `app-tenant.html`'s partial Capacitor bundle retires only once its successor instance is actually named and proven against the fixture corpus, and only once unresolved decision D10 is settled. The orphaned native stylesheet is not among this group's four rows; it is `S-481` and travels with O07.
remain: `404.html` stays exactly as it is and is explicitly not retired — it becomes a capability, with its `ErrorDocument 404` wiring intact in both `.htaccess` variants. What the signature still owes on that row is the capability itself: it is "to be named", it sits in K8/K10/K11, and parity means the capability is reachable from chat in every channel that offers it today. `offline.html` stays in place until K16 and stays unable to fire; restoring offline support would require adding a `fetch` handler, which the service worker's own comments refuse on principle, so this is a deliberate architectural choice rather than an oversight to repair. The evidenced owner recorded on `app-tenant.html` (StatusBar, Keyboard, App/appUrlOpen) and its dependency on D10 remain on the record until a successor instance is named.
risk: LOW-MEDIUM, and the three retirements do not carry equal weight. `vkid-sdk.js` is genuinely free: parity risk recorded as none, zero references, no capability to lose. `offline.html` carries no parity risk either — it cannot fire — but it is a live deployed artifact in four Beget manifests, so retiring it is a host-side operation rather than a repository delete. `app-tenant.html` is the row that needs care: it is identity-bearing (`X-Telegram-InitData` at four sites), its successor instance is not yet named, and it depends on unresolved decision D10. The fourth row is not a retirement at all; its only recorded hazard is collateral — `ErrorDocument 404` is wired at «сайт и приложение/.htaccess»:5 and `htaccess-root.txt`:5, so an htaccess consolidation during relay retirement could drop one directive and leave a bare server error page on that vhost. Signing changes nothing today — the retirements sit in K16 and the 404 capability work in K8/K10/K11 — but none of it may be executed as routine cleanup.
user_impact:
Signing G18 changes nothing for anyone. All four rows are packaged for later — S-659 is "NOT RETIRED", S-662 and S-668 are "RETIRE IN K16, row by row", S-490 is K16 — and the dossier's own signing block says approval brings "no production change. No deployed byte changes." The proposed text reads as if three of the four deletions land now; none of them does.

When the K16 pass does run, per row: `404.html` (S-659) is the group's one demonstrably live client-facing surface — it is wired by `ErrorDocument 404 /404.html` in both «сайт и приложение/.htaccess»:5 and `htaccess-root.txt`:5 (verified) and fires today for any client hitting a bad URL — and it is not retired, so it stays as it is; the one user-visible failure mode to guard is collateral, an `.htaccess` consolidation during relay retirement dropping one of the two `ErrorDocument` directives and leaving a bare server error page on that vhost. `offline.html` (S-662) cannot be served as an offline fallback, because the active service worker deliberately registers no `fetch` handler (its own comments at lines 2 and 24, grep-confirmed) — but "unreachable" is scoped to that mechanism, not to the file: it is live on the host as `app/offline.html` under `mayaos.ru` in the Beget public hash manifest (2,669 bytes), so it stays directly addressable by URL and its deletion is a host-tree plus manifest change, not a repo-only no-op. Drop the claim that "no client has ever been shown it" — the evidence covers the current SW, not history, and cannot be checked either way. `vkid-sdk.js` (S-668) is referenced by no code anywhere in the repo (repo-wide grep finds only doc mentions in CLAUDE.md, ROADMAP.md and the dossiers), so deleting 169,847 bytes changes nothing on screen — with the same host caveat, since the deployed copy is `mayaos.ru/app/vkid-sdk.js` in that hash manifest. `app-tenant.html` (S-490) does not move at all: its retirement is gated on a named successor proven against the fixture corpus and on unresolved decision D10.
security_impact:
Direction is right on the one real item, but the improvement is contingent and much narrower than claimed, and one sentence of the proposal is affirmatively wrong.

Contingent: signing removes nothing, so there is no security delta in this wave — the gain arrives only if K16 executes. When it does, deleting `vkid-sdk.js` (S-668) removes ~170 KB of unreferenced third-party VK OAuth client code from a publicly served path (`mayaos.ru/app/vkid-sdk.js`, 169,847 bytes in the Beget public hash manifest; the file makes credentialed cross-origin `fetch` calls to the VK OAuth endpoint and calls `window.open`). That is a genuine supply-chain reduction, and "removes nothing load-bearing" survives — in fact more strongly than the row states, since a repo-wide grep finds no code reference at all, not merely none in `app.html`, `index.html` and `tips.html`. Caveat: the row's reference check covers the malesthetic bundles, while the deployed copy lives in the `mayaos.ru` public tree next to `mayaos/app/oauth-callback.html`; that tree and its hash manifest must be re-checked before deletion, exactly the correction S-662 already needed.

Wrong as written: deleting this file does NOT "clear the standing no VK/MAX policy violation." The live VK surface is elsewhere and untouched by this group — `app.html`, the production PWA, carries a full VK ID PKCE login flow that POSTs to `PROXY?action=vk_auth` and writes `web_session_token` into localStorage (~L40887); `app-tenant.html` does the same (~L22848); the Beget relay dispatches both `vk_auth` and `vk_sdk_auth`; `webhook_server.py` registers live `/api/auth/vk` and `/api/auth/vk-sdk` routes (L9954–9957); and `web_auth.py`'s VK path can escalate a VK identity into a staff session through `VK_STAFF_CHAT_MAP`, as its own security comment records. The row's own note also lists `app-data.json` still carrying `"max": "#"`. So the deletion removes the single inert fragment of the VK surface and leaves every identity-bearing part in place — the risk here is not the deletion, it is reading it as VK being closed.

No server-side authority check, tenant boundary, consent record or audit trail lives in these four rows, so nothing client-side is removed that a server gate must replace. Two holds stand: `app-tenant.html` (S-490) injects `X-Telegram-InitData` at four sites and is identity-bearing, so its later retirement is an identity change, not a cosmetic bundle deletion; and S-659's note flags that an `.htaccess` consolidation during relay retirement could drop one of the two `ErrorDocument 404` directives, leaving a bare server default error page — an availability and server-banner-disclosure regression, so "no regressions" holds only if that directive pair is preserved. Nothing here touches the frozen limitations (fail-closed 13/21, STEP_UP unreachable, Gate 10 measured-not-enforced, approval role-gated rather than separation-of-duties, GAP-ATTENDANCE-CONFIRM open).
